Re: Ms Sally McConville, aged 38



   I am writing to urgently refer the above patient, who has been diagnosed with acute asthma with            Comment [OET3]: indentation is not wrong
suspected pneumonia. She requires your immediate assessment and management.                                   but it is preferable to omit it
                                                                                                              Comment [OET4]: Ms McConville: it is
                                                                                                              preferable to name the patient

Today, Ms McConville presented with worsening shortness of breath despite using the previously
prescribed medications. Her vital signs were raised, and she was found to be febrile and using her            Comment [OET5]: this is not clear to the
accessory muscles while breathing. On examination, widespread wheezing and bi-basal crepitations were         reader you are confusing him as you never
                                                                                                              mentioned anything about these medications.
persistent. Consequently, she was commenced on salbutamol nebulization 5mg; however, it did not
improve her condition.                                                                                        Comment [OET6]: pulse and respiratory
                                                                                                              rate: not all vitals were raised.
                                                                                                              Comment [OET7]: do not put comma after
                                                                                                              and if the two fragments are related and the
Initially, on 10/09/14, she visited the hospital with clinical features of an infective exacerbation of her   fragment before it is short
asthma secondary to a viral upper respiratory tract infection. Subsequently, 2 days later, she presented
                                                                                                              Comment [OET8]: used: use the past to
with a 1-day history of exertional shortness of breath and wheezing, accompanied by a fever and               report vital signs and lab results
yellowish sputum. On her chest auscultation, widespread wheezing was heard. As such, amoxicillin
                                                                                                              Comment [OET9]: Ms McConville: do not
500mg, three times a day and prednisolone 25mg, once a day for 3 days were prescribed. Additionally,          start the paragraph with she/he
she was advised to continue using fluticasone 250, 2 puffs daily with Ventolin, 2 puffs 4 hourly.
                                                                                                              Comment [OET10]: it is preferable to write
                                                                                                              the numbers from 1 to 10 in words
Regarding her medical history, she has asthma, hypertension and depression for which she takes ramipril,
paroxetine, fluticasone and salbutamol, 2 puffs as required, respectively.                                    Comment [OET11]: Thus,
                                                                                                              Comment [OET12]: This is not respectively
[It would be greatly appreciated if you could] carry out further assessment and management of suspected
pneumonia of this patient.                                                                                    Comment [OET13]: Ms Mcconville: don’t
                                                                                                              use patient you should use the name more


If you have any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.



Yours sincerely,                                                                                              Comment [OET14]: faithfully,

Doctor
